premises.text: CPG marketers waste half of huge ad/coupon budgets for lack of targeting—cannot tell switchers from loyalists and still print mass Sunday coupons
premises.evidence_span: they know 50% of that budget is misspent and wasted on the wrong customers. The trouble is, they don't know which 50%

premises.text: Snapdragon is a product barcode check-in game: zap, share to Facebook/Twitter, see friends' opinions in-store at decision time, plus Fanship leaderboards
premises.evidence_span: Snapdragon is a product check-in game with a twist

premises.text: Twist engagement: sarcastic dragon quips and comic-book adventures unlocked by product check-in combinations
premises.evidence_span: as you check into different combinations of products, you unlock these comic books

premises.text: Gives consumer product marketers the targeting tools they need wrapped in the gaming experience
premises.evidence_span: By finally giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need, and wrapping the whole thing in this fun gaming experience

value.text: Reinvention of how consumer product companies market to customers via targeted, fun engagement
value.evidence_span: fundamentally reinvent how consumer product companies market to their customers

causal_links.evidence_span: This is the opportunity here for disruption
It's product check-ins that unlock a comic book adventure
giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need

notes: Wasted coupons/no targeting/print media folded as one CPG targeting problem (§4.1.6). Check-in+social+Fanship cascade with quips/comics as the named twist kept as product mechanism (§4.1.7); marketer targeting claim kept as separately stated GTM/value path for brands. $2.2T disruption framing is vision—coded via value not as premise (§4.1.4).
